# New renderings — iliad-041 (7.1–91)

Rows for the table in `conventions.md`. No departure from a published rendering was needed; the lines the packet
showed (7.18, 7.28, 7.33, 7.40, 7.43, 7.49, 7.51, 7.55, 7.67, 7.68) keep the English they have there, and 7.33,
7.66b and 7.91a (whole units already published) are identical to the published units.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὴν πρότερος προσέειπεν ἄναξ Διὸς υἱὸς Ἀπόλλων (7.23, whole-line speech introduction) | "Her first addressed the lord, the son of Zeus, Apollo:" | "Lord Apollo, the son of Zeus, spoke to her first:" | "king", "prince" (ἄναξ is "lord" as in the table); "answered" (kept for ἀμείβομαι) |
| τὴν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπεν ἄναξ Διὸς υἱὸς Ἀπόλλων (7.37, whole-line reply introduction) | "Her then in turn addressed the lord, the son of Zeus, Apollo:" | "Then lord Apollo, the son of Zeus, spoke to her in turn:" | as above; the shipped τὴν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε pattern, with αὖτε "in turn" |
| κορυνήτης (Ἀρηΐθοος, 7.9) | "club-wielder" | "the club-wielder" | "club-man", "mace-bearer", "club-bearer"; κορύνη "club" |
| λύντο δὲ γυῖα (7.12, 7.16; death formula) | "and his limbs were loosened" | "and his limbs gave way" | "were unstrung", "failed", "went slack"; keeps "loosened" of λέλυνται (7.6) in `l` |
| ὑπὸ στεφάνης εὐχάλκου (7.12) | "beneath the well-bronzed rim" | "under the rim of fine bronze" (+ note: the helmet’s rim) | "crest", "ridge" (decide the helmet’s part), "of the helmet" in `i` (not in the Greek) |
| Δεξιάδην (Ἰφίνοον Δεξιάδην, 7.15) | "Dexiades" | "Dexiades" (+ note: patronymic, father not named in this part) | "son of Dexios" (names a father the Greek does not give) |
| ἑλέτην (7.8, dual of αἱρέω of men in battle) | "the two took" | "the two killed" | follows ἑλέτην in iliad-032 (5.576); "captured", "seized" |
| ἑτεραλκέα νίκην (7.26) | "a victory in battle, other-strengthening" | "a victory in battle that turns the fight to the other side" (+ note: built on ἕτερος and ἀλκή) | "decisive", "reversing", "fickle"; ἑτεραλκής is glossed "giving strength to the other side" |
| διαπραθέειν (διαπέρθω, 7.32) | "to sack through and through" | "to sack" | "to sack-utterly" (kept for ἐκπέρσαι), "to ravage", "to plunder"; ἄστυ is "town" as in the shipped lines |
| ὣς φίλον ἔπλετο θυμῷ (7.31) | "so it has been dear to the spirit" | "it has so pleased the spirit of" | "it is the will of" (the Odyssey table avoids "will"), "your hearts are set on" |
| τέκμωρ (Ἰλίου, 7.30–31; "end") | "an end of Ilios" | "an end for Ilios" (+ note: at 1.526 the same word is a "sign") | "doom", "the fated end", "term"; the shipped "sign" (1.526) and "way out"/"end" (Odyssey) |
| ἑκάεργε (vocative, 7.34) | "far-working one" | "you who work from afar" | "far-shooter", "archer"; the table’s ἑκάεργος "far-working" / "who works from afar" |
| χαλκοκνήμιδες Ἀχαιοί (7.41) | "bronze-greaved Achaeans" | "bronze-greaved Achaeans" | "bronze-shinned", "bronze-armoured" (χαλκοχίτωνες is "bronze-shirted"); κνημίς "greave" as in ἐϋκνήμιδες |
| ἀγασσάμενοι (7.41; ἀγάομαι "wonder at" or "be indignant at", here the second) | "feeling indignation" | "feeling indignation" (+ note: sense chosen from context) | "in wonder" (the other sense), "resenting", "taking offence" |
| οἰόθεν οἶος (7.39) | "singly, alone" | "all alone" | "by himself alone", "one against one" |
| Διὶ μῆτιν ἀτάλαντε (7.47) | "to Zeus in cunning equal" | "the equal of Zeus in cunning" | "in counsel" (μῆτις is "cunning"), "match", "peer"; follows the table's Διὶ μῆτιν ἀτάλαντον (2.169) |
| σύνθετο θυμῷ βουλήν (7.44) | "put together in spirit the plan" | "grasped in his spirit the plan" | "took to heart", "laid up in mind"; συντίθεμαι "put together", i.e. understand |
| μοῖρα θανεῖν καὶ πότμον ἐπισπεῖν (7.52) | "fate to die and to meet your doom" | "your fate to die and meet your doom" | "destiny"; μοῖρα "fate", πότμος "doom", ἐπισπεῖν "meet" as in the shipped ἐπίσπῃ |
| ὄρνισιν ἐοικότες αἰγυπιοῖσι (7.59) | "likened to birds, to vultures" | "like birds, like vultures" | "eagles", "falcons"; αἰγυπιός "vulture" as in the Odyssey |
| φρὶξ Ζεφύροιο (7.63) | "the ripple of the West Wind" | "the ripple of the West Wind" | "shiver", "ruffling", "Zephyr" (the Odyssey table’s "West Wind"); φρίξ is the surface ripple |
| Τροίην εὔπυργον (7.71) | "Troy, the well-towered" | "well-towered Troy" | "high-towered", "of the fine towers"; εὖ + πύργος, matching "well-walled" for εὐτείχεος |
| τεκμαίρεται (7.70) | "fixes matters" | "fixes matters" | "ordains", "decrees" (turned down at τεκμήραντο 6.349), "plans", "devises"; follows the table's τεκμαίρομαι "fix" |
| κακὰ φρονέων (7.70) | "thinking evils" | "with evil in his mind" | "plotting", "scheming" (each drops φρήν); follows the shipped φίλα φρονέων "thinking kindly" |
| πρόμος (7.75) | "champion" | "champion" | "foremost fighter", "front-fighter" (kept for πρόμαχος) |
| ἐπιμάρτυρος (7.76) | "witness" | "witness" | "overseer", "guarantor" |
| ταναήκεϊ χαλκῷ (7.77) | "long-pointed bronze" | "long-pointed bronze" | "long-edged", "keen-edged", "lengthy-bladed"; ἀκή "point, edge", ταναός "long" |
| πυρός … λελάχωσι (7.79–80) | "may give a share of fire" | "may give me my share of fire" | "may burn", "may grant the rites"; the reduplicated aorist of λαγχάνω is causative |
| εὖχος … δώῃ (7.81) | "give me a boast" | "grants me the triumph" | "glory" (κλέος, κῦδος); follows iliad-033 ("boast" in `l`, "triumph" in `i`) |
| ταρχύσωσι (7.85) | "may bury" | "may bury" (+ note: funeral word, origin not known) | "entomb", "give funeral rites"; no derivation is claimed |
| σῆμα … χεύωσιν (7.86, 7.89; grave-mound) | "heap up a tomb" · "the tomb" | "heap up a tomb" · "the tomb" | "mound", "barrow", "sign"; follows the shipped "tomb" for σῆμα (iliad-015, 2.814) |
| Ἑλλήσποντος (πλατεῖ Ἑλλησπόντῳ, 7.86) | "the broad Hellespont" | "the broad Hellespont" | "Hellespont strait", "wide Helle’s sea" |
| νηῒ πολυκλήϊδι (7.88) | "a many-thwarted ship" | "a ship of many thwarts" | "many-oared", "many-benched" (kept for πολυζύγῳ); follows the shipped πολυκλήϊσι |
| ὀψιγόνων ἀνθρώπων (7.87) | "men born later" | "men born later" | "men of later generations", "descendants"; follows the Odyssey’s ὀψιγόνων "born later" |
| ὅν ποτ’ ἀριστεύοντα κατέκτανε (7.90) | "whom once, as he excelled, … killed" | "whom … once killed while he was excelling" | "as the best", "in his prime"; ἀριστεύω keeps "be the best" (6.208) |
| τὸ δ’ ἐμὸν κλέος οὔ ποτ’ ὀλεῖται (7.91) | "and my fame never will perish" | "and my fame will never perish" | "glory" (the phrase κλέος οὔ ποτ’ ὀλεῖται stands at 2.325 as "fame will never perish" and keeps that English) |
| ἐϋξέστῃς ἐλάτῃσι (7.5) | "well-polished fir-oars" | "well-polished fir-oars" | "planed", "smooth oars of fir"; follows the Odyssey’s ξεστῇς ἐλάτῃσιν "polished fir-oars" |
| οὖρον (ναύτῃσιν … ἔδωκεν οὖρον, 7.4–5) | "a fair wind" | "a fair wind" | "favouring wind" (reserved for ἴκμενον); follows the shipped Odyssey lines |
